supports: consumeRememberMeCookie splits the cookie value into series and token and loads the persistent token by series
it verifies the token value but never compares persistentToken->getUserIdentifier() or getClass() with the cookie user identifier/class
it then calls parent::consumeRememberMeCookie with a value that keeps the cookie-supplied user identifier
the parent loads the user with userProvider->loadUserByIdentifier($rememberMeDetails->getUserIdentifier())
the identifier therefore comes from the cookie, so without the owner check the token of one account authenticates the account named in the edited cookie
fromRawCookie decodes up to four delimited parts: user FQCN, base64 user identifier, expiry and value
the user identifier is attacker-editable text in the cookie, subject only to base64 decoding
the fixed handler compares persistentToken->getUserIdentifier() and getClass() with the cookie values and throws AuthenticationException on mismatch
it rebuilds RememberMeDetails from the persistent token instead of trusting the cookie fields
it also splits series:token with a limit of 2
the patch adds the owner comparison and unsets the untrusted details object
the patch changes PersistentRememberMeHandler.php and its test only

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No Symfony runtime, authentication listener, or PoC was executed; the finding is static.

The attacker model assumes the attacker can obtain a valid series/token pair for some account (for example their own) and can edit the cookie identifier field; the security advisory describes this as authentication bypass but does not publish an exploit.
The advisory gives ranges only for the 5.x/6.x/7.x branches; other maintained branches were not audited.
NVD has no primary CVSS metric; the 7.5 vector is the GitHub advisory (GitHub_M CNA) metric, recorded as secondary by NVD.

critical_operation.description: consumeRememberMeCookie loads the persisted token by series and validates its token value, but never checks that the token row belongs to the user identifier and user class carried in the cookie. The parent handler then loads the user by the cookie-supplied identifier, so an attacker holding any valid series/token pair can change the identifier field to another account and be authenticated as that account. The 5.4.47 fix adds the owner comparison and rebuilds the details from the stored token.

entry_point.description: The remember-me authentication listener calls consumeRememberMeCookie with RememberMeDetails parsed from the client cookie; the cookie user identifier is attacker-controlled (base64 text) and is trusted by the parent handler at AbstractRememberMeHandler.php:74.

trace.description: RememberMeDetails is parsed from the client cookie; the identifier is base64 text chosen by the client
consumeRememberMeCookie loads the persistent token by series and verifies only the token value, not the owner
The parent loads the user by the cookie-supplied identifier and returns it as authenticated

location.verification_method: Static read of PersistentRememberMeHandler.php, AbstractRememberMeHandler.php and RememberMeDetails.php at v5.4.45 and v5.4.47, the fix diff, the advisory and git tag ancestry; no code executed.
